comments.text:
If they were capable people they would have built a rail  road system decades ago, but sub-Saharan Africans aren't even capable of maintaining the infrastructure left to them by the Europeans. 

I hear people say African countries were "set back" by colonialism, but Kenya has been an independent nation since 1963. So how exactly is Kenya, or any other sub-Saharan African country still somehow being "set back" by colonialism today, when it ended more than 60 years ago? 

Several East Asian countries were also colonized, and every single one of them are more prosperous than most European countries today? Many Southeast Asian countries were also colonized, and today those countries are either more prosperous than most European countries, or on an economic trajectory to surpass them by the end of this decade. So if colonialism has such long lasting negative repercussions, that it's still the cause of sub-Saharan Africa's inability to economically prosper, why does this phenomenon only seem to hinder sub-Saharan African countries?

I'll tell you why, it's because blaming Africa's problems on colonialism is bullsh*t. Africa's problems today are a direct result of the people who live there. Sub-Saharan Africa's problems are about what should be expected from an entire continent full of people whose resting pulse rate is significantly higher than their average IQ.
